features.title: User lifecycle and email/password
features.appliesTo: Authentication / Identity Platform; client and Admin REST; configured project
limitations: Broad route and lifetime invariants only; atomic per-operation source mappings and target-version observations remain open. Real email/SMS delivery and anti-abuse are separate boundaries.

features.title: Tokens and sessions
features.appliesTo: Authentication; Secure Token and Admin verification paths; project/tenant binding
limitations: Revocation behavior must be checked separately for each verifier and service; no release-specific evidence is attached.

features.title: Authentication account lifecycle
features.appliesTo: Identity Toolkit REST; configured project; Admin owner and authenticated client subjects
limitations: The pinned conformance fixtures are official Local Emulator Suite observations; production account lifecycle parity remains a candidate until matching project, input and observer identities are recorded.
Session cookies, out-of-band actions, MFA and external provider protocol exchange are outside this finite lifecycle slice.

features.title: TOTP enrollment and sign-in
features.appliesTo: Identity Platform; explicit auth.totp configuration; supported verified first factor; tenant-specific settings
limitations: The existing Auth production corpus has no TOTP program. Linked invariants do not yet cover all eligibility, unenrollment and provider constraints.

features.title: SMS multi-factor authentication
features.appliesTo: Identity Platform; configured MFA and first-factor eligibility
limitations: Local verification codes do not attest real SMS delivery, retries, anti-abuse or production MFA configuration.

features.title: Tenant isolation and configuration
features.appliesTo: Identity Platform; project and tenant client/Admin REST routes
limitations: Per-tenant provider, MFA and policy combinations need additional source and oracle mappings.

features.title: Federated provider configuration and fixture assertions
features.appliesTo: Project/tenant OAuth IdP and inbound SAML configuration CRUD plus local fixture assertion handling; live OAuth/OIDC/SAML protocol and provider verification are distinct
limitations: A fake JWT or JSON SAML assertion is not a real provider credential exchange.
Local provider configuration CRUD does not establish a live external-provider flow or production response parity.

features.title: Blocking authentication functions
features.appliesTo: Identity Platform; configured before-create and before-sign-in hooks
limitations: Hook ordering, rollback and configuration need source-section and live-oracle review.

features.title: Document reads, writes and queries
features.appliesTo: Firestore Standard / Native; per-database rules, indexes and profile; REST and gRPC considered separately
limitations: The broad parity requirement is not full method/field/enum coverage. Commit atomicity and BatchWrite partial outcomes must not be conflated.

features.title: Count, sum and average
features.appliesTo: Firestore Standard / Native; query/index configuration; REST and gRPC
limitations: Historical queries/aggregations corpus observations exist but are not accepted for this source tree. Streaming equivalence is not a substitute for production semantics.

features.title: Transactions and contention
features.appliesTo: Standard / Native; configured concurrency mode must be read back; transaction tokens and retry paths
limitations: Edition does not determine the observed database concurrency mode. Exact timeout, retry and ordering assertions remain to be mapped.

features.title: Listen and stream lifecycle
features.appliesTo: Standard / Native; gRPC Listen and SDK WebChannel; reconnect/resume behavior
limitations: Resource bounds do not establish event completeness, order or all resume histories. REST availability must not be inferred from stream support.

features.title: Rules and index configuration
features.appliesTo: Standard / Native; per-database rules/index catalog; request authentication and budgets
limitations: Standard index requirements cannot be transferred unconditionally to Enterprise. Refusal assertions must inspect unchanged state.

features.title: Pipeline validation and finite local read execution
features.appliesTo: Enterprise / Native; owner-authorized local latest reads of a collection, collection group or documents input through where, select, sort, add_fields, remove_fields, distinct, aggregate, offset and limit stages
limitations: A collection, collection_group or documents input followed by where, select, sort, add_fields, remove_fields, distinct, aggregate, offset and limit stages, each any number of times in any order, execute locally on the pipeline executor over rows read at one read version (FS-ENT-ORACLE O-6 and O-7, production, Enterprise, 2026-10-26, matched except the rows the replay test names with their reasons, which it compares row by row). Aggregates are count, count_distinct, sum, average, minimum and maximum. Expressions are field references (nested paths included), __name__, literals, the six comparisons, and, or, not, xor, nor, exists, is_absent, is_error, type, is_type, array_contains, array_contains_all, array_contains_any, equal_any and not_equal_any, array and map construction and document_id / collection_id / parent of a document reference. FS-ENT-ORACLE O-1 to O-4 (production, Enterprise, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20) answered every comparison, construction, alias, select-width, literal, map-key, document-function, limit/offset and where-condition probe it was given as the official emulator does (every pair of kinds, vectors by length first and missing fields included; integers and doubles exactly as one kind; the select alias length limit of 1500 UTF-8 bytes on the unquoted joined path; argument checks of unrun stages in the recorded orders). Both profiles answer those alike. What production has not answered (a collection reference with a non-ASCII name; a key that is not a plain name in a literal holding an expression; document-function argument types other than string, integer, map and boolean; map keys other than integer and boolean; malformed or integer vectors; several empty or reserved literal keys and the key __name__; limit types other than integer and string, offsets other than a non-negative integer and a string; fireemu's own argument-count and option texts; an empty map or a later check after a function or stage value fireemu does not check; documents paths other than a collection and a document) is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED under strict and answered as the official emulator answers it under the emulator profile. A field equality is applied by the scan without index validation (Enterprise needs no index; pending production observation). A run-time refusal may follow partial results; rows after a used-up limit are not evaluated. The same subset runs over REST :executePipeline (the Web SDK Lite transport); a REST refusal answers no partial results. Without a select a result is the whole source document (name and times); every response carries the snapshot read time as executionTime. Known differences from production: the groups of an aggregate come in the order they were first met, where production's is its own and unobserved (so a limit, an offset or a sort with tied keys after the groups can differ), and a limit after a sort cuts a group of rows tied on every sort key in an order the scan order does not explain; an unsorted read is in production's scan order, ascending CRC-32 of the document IDs. A larger answer is cut into responses or array elements at about 1 MiB of results; production cuts a larger answer into units of 5 to 199 results (2 KB to 37 KB) whose boundaries differ between two reads of the same data (500 small documents came in 3 to 9 units, 5000 in 26 to 40; a document of 400 KB or more is a unit of its own and 100 KB documents come two to a unit), and put every recorded answer of 50 small documents or fewer in one response or element (FS-ENT-ORACLE O-8A); fireemu's cut differs. Offset skips filtered rows once across the existing paged stream. The stages union, unnest, sample, find_nearest, replace_with and the database input, regex functions, the remaining math functions, timestamp and map function families and consistency selectors remain unsupported. The recorded string functions concat, to_lower, to_upper, starts_with, ends_with, string_contains, char_length, substring, trim, ltrim, rtrim and split and math functions add, subtract, multiply, divide, mod, abs, round, floor, ceil and pow run locally for their supported shapes. Production behavior is observed only as the FS-ENT-ORACLE recordings O-1 to O-9b took it (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-27: the stage grammar and its refusal texts, sort and stage order, where-context answers, aggregate, distinct, add_fields, remove_fields, collection_group, documents, the order of a read without a sort, the string, math, timestamp, map and array function families, union, unnest, sample, is_type over every type name and the response framing); the string and math families include locally supported shapes; regex, timestamp, map and array functions, union, unnest and sample include recorded shapes not run locally. Not observed: error precedence on the Standard (default) database and for a non-owner caller, base64 decoding in createDocument, patch and batchWrite, non-ASCII document IDs and CRC-32 ties, and is_type of a vector. Production answers two shapes with an HTTP 500 INTERNAL that fireemu does not reproduce: an alias repeated in quotes and array_reverse() with no argument. Parser acceptance is not execution support.

features.title: Text index lifecycle and finite local lexical search
features.appliesTo: Enterprise / Native; local text catalog, explicit build controls and collection/search latest reads
limitations: Local lexical-v1 analysis and approximate BM25 are not production-equivalent; productionExact refuses search until production comparison is recorded. Transactions, geo search, language morphology, enhancement and general search expression trees remain unsupported. Purpose-specific scalar-local Latin diacritic folding is a bounded development approximation, not a recovered native analyzer; CJK segmentation, ranking and broader Unicode analysis remain unverified.

features.title: MongoDB-compatible API and drivers
features.appliesTo: Firestore with MongoDB compatibility; published supported API/type/driver set still to inventory
limitations: Unmapped: no Standard/Native or generic MongoDB compatibility result transfers to this goal.

features.title: Database, index and retention administration
features.appliesTo: Database/index administration; TTL, backup/restore, PITR, import/export and operation lifecycle
limitations: Admin discovery fields and long-running operation semantics remain unclassified; configuration acceptance does not imply managed-service execution.

features.title: Client and Admin SDK behavior
features.appliesTo: Web/Node client and Admin SDKs; offline/cache/listeners and auth handoff; mobile platforms separately inventoried
limitations: The linked rules-unit-testing requirement covers one integration path only. Offline, pending writes, mobile SDKs and target-version runs remain unmapped.

features.title: Managed cloud operations and external providers
features.appliesTo: Real IAM, billing, regions, CMEK, email/SMS, IdPs, network and anti-abuse services
limitations: Local response/configuration simulation does not reproduce cloud operations. External dependencies remain visible and must be verified separately.
